newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Mysterious missing rebel obsesses Guatemala.
newsitem.headline: Mysterious missing rebel obsesses Guatemala.

text.p: The fate of a mysterious missing guerrilla who may be the final casualty of a 36-year rebellion has become a national obsession in Guatemala, where a hard-won peace has not yet quieted the ghosts of civil war.

Newspapers here are full of stories alleging that a shadowy figure known as Commander Mincho was tortured and killed by the army late last year after he was caught taking part in a rebel-led kidnapping.
The Mincho affair is a potential embarrassment for both the former rebels and the government because it is reminiscent of the kind of dirty tactics that both sides have pledged to abandon.
Adding to the mystery, the government and former guerrilla leaders, in a rare show of unity, say Mincho never existed.
"Mincho is a story invented by someone who suffers from insomnia," presidential spokesman Ricardo de la Torre said in one of many emphatic denials.

But the U.N. human rights mission here began an investigation and tentatively identified Mincho as a former guerrilla named Juan Jose Cabrera, who did disappear and may have been involved in the kidnapping.

"It is presumed that they are the same person, but it has not been proven. We are collecting information and still need to interview some people who could have information," Carlos Urrutia of the United Nations Mission for the Verification of Human Rights in Guatemala (MINUGUA) told Reuters on Monday.

At the time Mincho allegedly died, the government and rebel leaders of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) were in the final, tense stretch of peace talks. A ceasefire had been in effect for months.

Guerrillas had supposedly ceased kidnapping and other illegal "fund-raising" operations, and the civilian government of President Alvaro Arzu had presumably renounced the ways of torture and assassination of past military regimes.

The kidnap victim, Olga de Novella, 86, matriarch of a wealthy family, was rescued by the army. Mincho supposedly was captured during the operation. Arzu suspended the peace talks for two weeks until URNG leaders made public apologies.
Both sides went on to sign a peace accord on Dec. 29.
